chunks: Hanan ibn Sadir narrated from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

A mawla of Ali عليه السلام died, so he said, 'Look and see whether you can find an heir for him.' It was said to him that he had two daughters in al-Yamamah who were enslaved. So he purchased them from the wealth of the deceased, then gave them the remainder of the inheritance.

key_terms.بَقِيَّةَ الْمِيرَاثِ: the remainder of the inheritance after the purchase
key_terms.بِالْيَمَامَةِ: in al-Yamamah, the location where the daughters were found
key_terms.مَالِ الْمَيِّتِ: the estate or wealth left by the deceased
key_terms.وَارِثًا: a legal heir entitled to inherit

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali عليه السلام deal with the inheritance of a deceased person whose heirs were enslaved daughters?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that when a servant associated with Imam Ali عليه السلام died, the Imam sought out his legal heirs rather than letting the estate go unclaimed. Upon learning that the deceased had two enslaved daughters, he had them purchased from the deceased's estate and then gave them the remaining inheritance, reflecting rulings related to inheritance and the legal status of enslaved heirs.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5732 - Hanan ibn Sadir narrated from Ibn Abi Yafur from Ishaq ibn Ammar from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) who said:

"A servant of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) passed away.
Imam Ali (as) said: 'Look and see if he has any heirs.'
It was said to Him (as): 'He has two daughters in Yamamah who are enslaved.'
So, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) purchased them using the deceased's wealth and then gave them the remainder of the inheritance."
